claims.title: Two-sided interchange smoothing proposes polynomial-bit endpoint sampling by rate saturation

status: source_derived_unreviewed; Unreviewed source-reported mathematical proof candidate. Intake checks source bytes, derived page routes and repository integrity, not independent correctness or novelty. No scientific script execution, sampler implementation, benchmark, formal verification or physical experiment. Historical priority and external correctness UNKNOWN.
interface: For an explicitly supplied undirected graph with n vertices and m edges, nonnegative binary-rational exchange rates w_e, deterministic initial permutation (or multicolor/exclusion configuration), nonnegative binary-rational horizon T and accuracy 0<epsilon<=1, the manuscript proposes a classical sampler of one full endpoint within total-variation epsilon of the continuous-time interchange law. At each edge clock, endpoint labels exchange without bias or configuration-dependent rate. The claimed bit cost is polynomial in n,m,input bit lengths and 1/epsilon, independent of numerical T and original rates; it does not enumerate n! states or reconstruct joint law from one-particle marginals. This is a proof candidate, not implemented or benchmarked capability. The graph and rates are supplied explicitly, not succinctly encoded or physically acquired for free.
limits: Independently reconstruct the weighted discrepancy coupling, killed-pair Green bound including disconnected graphs, group-inversion row gradient, involution factorization and uniform two-sided Duhamel integration. Audit all constants and edge-by-edge capping, finite rational categorical/rejection budgets and worst-case bit cost; implement and benchmark full endpoints against exact small cases and strong matched samplers. Review historical priority separately; calibrate physical rates/model before material-specific use.
